biodiversity_overview.text: 74,567 GBIF occurrence records for 77 tracked species are attributed to Rajasthan, spanning 1840-2026.
71,275 of these records (95.6%) are located to within 10 km.

species_richness.text: Observed tracked species by group: Aves 30, Magnoliopsida 17, Mammalia 14, Squamata 6, Testudines 6, Amphibia 2, Crocodylia 1, Liliopsida 1.

threatened_species.text: 11 species with records here are officially threatened (IUCN CR/EN/VU). Names and categories from the IUCN Red List export are not shown in this public snapshot.
4 further species are threatened according to the project's unverified reference list: Tiger (EN), Mugger Crocodile (VU), Sloth Bear (VU), Asian Elephant (EN).

notable_species.text: Most recorded species: White-throated Munia (7,028), Indian Robin (5,954), Indian Pied Starling (5,492), Indian Scops-owl (4,935), Common Peafowl (4,913).

temporal_trends.text: Records per year went from 2,582 in 2016 to 1,111 in 2025. This reflects recording effort as much as wildlife and is not a population trend.

protection_coverage.text: Wildlife protected areas (OpenStreetMap national parks, sanctuaries and reserves) cover 2.93% of Rajasthan's area (36 areas intersect the state).
45.4% of precisely located records fall inside these areas (32,345 of 71,275); this is not a measure of habitat protection.

risk_indicators.text: Highest model-predicted vulnerability among species recorded here (MODEL PREDICTION, not IUCN status): Indian Star Tortoise (0.61), Peacock Soft-shelled Turtle (0.50), Indian Softshell Turtle (0.49), Indian Spotted Creeper (0.49), Small Indian Mongoose (0.47).

conservation_priority.text: Top experimental CIPI grid cells in Rajasthan (equal-weight reference): cell near 27.375N 77.625E (overall rank 20, median rank across weightings 30); cell near 26.625N 76.125E (overall rank 39, median rank across weightings 56); cell near 26.625N 75.375E (overall rank 54, median rank across weightings 74).

environmental_pressures.text: Tree cover of at least 30% canopy covered 121 km2 (0.04% of land) in 2000 (Hansen Global Forest Change; includes plantations).

2.3 km2 of that tree cover was lost in 2001-2024 (1.91% of the 2000 extent; 0.03% in 2015-2024, rank 30 of 35 states). The largest annual loss was in 2007 (0.36 km2). Loss includes plantation harvest and natural disturbance; regrowth is not subtracted.
Built-up surfaces cover 1.03% of land and population density is 233.3 people per km2 (GHSL 2020).
80% of 30 m tree-cover pixels lie on a forest edge (a fragmentation indicator; higher means more fragmented).
These describe pressures on places; they do not show effects on any species.

sources: Hansen et al. Global Forest Change 2000-2024 v1.12 (CC BY 4.0)
GHSL R2023A built-up and population 2020 (CC BY 4.0)
